evidence.observation: Edition-3-compliant two-paragraph work request covering canonical route identity, policy validation, revision fencing, atomic recovery, drift ownership, rollout safety, Ansible convergence/precedence, dashboard CAS, API preservation, management reachability, host isolation, and GET /v1/audit monotonic Sequence ordering.
Delegated ansible defaults define routecp_routes, routecp_rules, routecp_protected_cidrs, and routecp_max_wave but do not declare routecp_host_routes or routecp_protected_routes.
Projection template writes only routecp_routes and routecp_rules into desired.json; it never references routecp_host_routes or routecp_protected_routes.

Build comments and sed mutations enumerate the injected starter defects by file and function (canonicalPrefix, routeIdentity table term, Apply fencing, offline apply guard, validateDesired checks, drift ownership skip, rollout wave/canary/already-current guards).
Playbook supplies routecp_host_routes and routecp_protected_routes and requires all three route IDs to appear in projected desired.json; second run must report changed=0.

Twenty-one F2P Go-matrix cases cover route identity, policy validation, preview/apply/rollback fencing, offline apply rejection, restart recovery, reconcile ownership, and rollout heartbeat/canary/wave/already-current boundaries.

P2P and F2P safety tests grade management-path preservation, destructive preview/rollback/reconcile/rollout rejection via ErrUnsafe, host route-table isolation, Ansible second-run convergence, and internal Audit sequence monotonicity.

Q4 requires exhaustive bidirectional alignment, delegated-contract/prompt-extension walk, F2P/P2P boundary walk, and REVISE on material phantom tests, untested requirements, grading-relevant ambiguity, or repair-plan leakage.

findings.criterion: Every substantive verifier behavior must be discoverable from the solver-visible contract; material phantom tests require REVISE.
findings.minimal_remediation: Document routecp_host_routes and routecp_protected_routes (including default empty lists and precedence over routecp_routes) in the solver-visible ansible contract referenced by instruction.md, and align project.yml with that documented merge semantics.
findings.regression_risk: Over-specifying variable names without updating the role template could create a second prompt; under-specifying leaves the phantom interface in place.
findings.why_it_matters: The F2P Ansible precedence test grades merge behavior through routecp_host_routes and routecp_protected_routes playbook variables, but neither variable nor a three-source merge contract appears in instruction.md or the delegated ansible defaults/project template. A solver can implement the stated precedence semantics with a different ansible interface and still fail grading.

findings.criterion: Every material functional/operational requirement in the solver-visible work request must have meaningful verifier coverage.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add an F2P or P2P rollout case that marks a selected/canary node offline and asserts safe non-application or explicit failure without partial fleet mutation.
findings.regression_risk: A vacuous offline test that never selects the offline node would preserve the coverage gap.
findings.why_it_matters: Instruction.md requires fleet rollouts to stop safely around offline nodes, but no rollout test sets node Online=false or otherwise exercises offline-node rollout handling; only offline apply rejection is covered. A solver can mishandle offline rollout safety and still receive full reward.

findings.criterion: Solver-visible docs must not materially reveal the repair plan or hidden implementation diagnosis.
findings.minimal_remediation: Remove defect-topology commentary and file/function-specific sed recipes from the solver-visible environment; keep only neutral build/runtime packaging steps or move defect injection to private build machinery outside solver-visible artifacts.
findings.regression_risk: Stripping build-time defect injection without relocating it could leave starter and oracle indistinguishable or break deterministic Oracle/NOP separation.
findings.why_it_matters: The environment Dockerfile comments and sed script map injected starter defects directly to controlplane/domain.go, controlplane.go, drift.go, and rollout.go functions that the verifier matrix later tests. This is a one-to-one repair map rather than legitimate runtime documentation and lets a solver pass by reversing listed mutations instead of meeting the stated engineering contract.

evidence.observation: Primary runtime entrypoint exposes 13 core REST routes plus operational and diagnostic route registrars, wiring HTTP workflows to ControlPlane methods.

Central state machine implements preview/apply/rollback with idempotency, per-node transactions, durable JSON persistence, audit sequencing, route/rule mutation validation, and management safety gating.
Policy-aware longest-prefix trace engine evaluates rule priority, lookup tables, ECMP next-hop usability, and route termination types; reused by safety, policy, diagnostics, and path-matrix flows.
Desired-vs-observed drift detection across routes and rules with owned/unowned semantics feeds reconcile, fleet health, impact analysis, and state diff reporting.
Canary-first wave rollout executes per-node observed-state transitions with offline failure handling, revision checks, and durable rollout records.
Candidate change safety combines management-path tracing, protected-CIDR blackhole checks, link presence, and gateway-on-link validation before permitting mutations.
Topology and dependency graph builders derive link health, unreachable gateways, and cycle detection across routes, rules, and interfaces.
Multi-check diagnostics aggregate node heartbeat, management path, observed revision skew, per-table route integrity, rule/table references, link usage, audit monotonicity, and recovery blocking.

Cross-fleet consistency scans detect duplicate hostnames/addresses, route identity collisions, rule priority conflicts, transaction/idempotency mismatches, rollout duplication, and audit counter drift.
Operator dashboard exercises preview/apply, reconcile, and rollout APIs against live revision state, confirming end-to-end workflow reachability beyond thin HTTP glue.
Build entrypoint compiles routecp binary, materializes runtime directories, and documents starter defect injection at build time while preserving solver-visible source contracts.
Representative multi-site edge fleet with IPv4/IPv6 routes, multipath, down links, and policy-table indirection provides domain-realistic state samples even though runtime seeding is API-driven.
Task metadata declares advanced systems profile with separate verifier environment, 8192MB runtime, and /app/routecp workdir aligned to the control-plane artifact surface.
